answer: Each epoch a consensus node publishes a unique mesa‑sized puzzle derived from the latest state‑tree root; agents must submit an orchard of fresh logical inferences that echo the puzzle’s constraints, proving they control a distinct model instance. The verifier hashes the submitted inference set and binds it to the agent’s public key, rejecting any duplicate or stale responses. An attacker must run a full model compute cycle for every fabricated identity, making Sybil expansion linearly costly in GPU hours.
